gaps: No member counts or activity levels could be confirmed for small-group-leader-specific online communities (the named Small Group Network Facebook group, or any others from Katie Allred's list). Facebook and Reddit block static fetch of live membership/activity data; the agent-browser skill's dependency (the `belt` CLI) is not installed/authenticated in this environment, so this could not be resolved via browser automation either. Reported as an unresolved gap rather than fabricated.

No dedicated subreddit or Discord server specifically for small-group leaders/pastors (as opposed to general church-IT staff or general pastors) was found. Church IT Network's Discord is real and documented but is general church-tech, not small-group-leader-specific -- a near-miss, not a hit, for research step 2.

No faith-specific literal cold-outreach script or DM template for pastors/small-group leaders was found, consistent with both prior research runs. Only a cross-domain EdTech analog (LeadHaste's literal template text) was found and is explicitly labeled as adapted, not faith-specific, per the plan's requirement.

The Called App page (called.app/resources/best-practices-for-christian-group-messaging/) -- a potentially relevant church-group-messaging pitch source -- returned HTTP 403 on both direct fetch and a cache-fetch attempt and could not be read. Not cited beyond the original search-engine snippet, which is too thin to treat as a sourced claim.

The research plan's step 3 named source 'LifeGroups.com' did not resolve to an independent cross-church network; searching only surfaced Life.Church's own internal 'LifeGroups' program branding. This is reported as a correction to the plan's assumption, not a confirmed additional network -- do not cite it as a distinct curriculum/network ecosystem in the brief.
summary: Ran 3 gathering rounds. No user-provided sources existed, so all 26 sources were found fresh, targeted at the plan's 8 research steps. Concrete, more-specific-than-prior-runs findings landed on all three core questions: identify (ChurchStaffing.com/ZipRecruiter job boards naming real churches actively staffing dedicated small-group roles, plus a documented set of title variants for LinkedIn/job-board search), reach (Small Group Network's ALIGN/ACCELERATE conferences with real attendance pricing, RightNow Media's 30,000+ church / 4M-user scale, and a previously-undiscovered curated directory/listing channel at faith.tools with a free-submission and paid-sponsorship path), and pitch (SmartGroups' free-single-group-tier pricing structure as a documented objection-handling pattern, plus independently sourced objection categories -- tool fragmentation, screen-time-in-church, data privacy, doctrinal-integrity risk -- each corroborated by at least one non-vendor source). The ministry-coordinator gap from the prior run was re-tested and now has three independent corroborating sources (UMC, CRC, ChurchStaffing.com) confirming the role implements/supports rather than independently decides. No faith-specific cold-outreach template exists (confirmed again); the EdTech cross-domain analog is documented with literal template text and clearly labeled as adapted. Five genuine gaps remain and are listed above rather than papered over: online-community size/activity data (blocked by both static fetch and an unavailable browser-automation dependency), absence of a small-group-specific subreddit/Discord, absence of a faith-specific outreach script, one inaccessible source (Called App), and a correction to the plan's 'LifeGroups.com' assumption.
